question: Ticket db250e9bf3f9 touches outline section 9.4.2.5.1, where Q#101 stands open: "proofgate reads the text of a Bash command, so a proof run from a script file ("bash run_it.sh", whose text names no proof) is invisible to it. Measured 2026-11-13: such a proof runs bare and writes into the live HOME/.cairn. Which should seal that spelling? (a) every proof refuses to run unless it is inside the tester's seal, as one check in a shared helper or at the scratch door; (b) the hook also reads the script file a bash/sh command names; (c) a proof run from a script file is accepted as outside the rule. CC leans (a): it is the only one that covers every spelling, not just the next one found. This reopens ticket 72a37498c601's WRONG INTENT clause; ticket dda0e72b9c67 clause 4 waits on it (open-49fc67a40ede)." What is the answer?
why_it_blocks: the ticket works inside outline section 9.4.2.5.1, and the answer to Q#101 may change it

notes.text: Measured 2026-11-16, CC: db250e9bf3f9 is bound to Q#101 because it touches the tester's verbs (outline 9.4.2.5, cairn test --reseal-install). Its build is a pre-merge-commit hook plus the installer, and its proof runs under the tester's seal. Every answer to Q#101, (a), (b) or (c), leaves that build unchanged, so this question needs no new answer of its own; the answer to Q#101 at open-49fc67a40ede closes it too.
